targetText: Every form of motion contains within itself its own particular contradiction. This particular contradiction constitutes the particular essence which distinguishes one thing from another.
explanation: Every field or subject has its own unique conflict that makes it what it is. Physics focuses on force vs. resistance; economics focuses on supply, demand, and labor value; personal relationships focus on intimacy vs. independence.

targetText: These are the two processes of cognition: one, from the particular to the general, and the other, from the general to the particular.
explanation: Learning works in a two-step cycle: first, you observe specific real-world examples to spot general patterns, and then you use those general patterns to solve new specific problems. Real-life example: Doctors examine many individual patients to learn how a virus works, then apply that general knowledge to treat new patients.

targetText: Qualitatively different contradictions can only be resolved by qualitatively different methods.
explanation: Different problems require completely different solutions. Real-life example: You fix a broken car engine with mechanical tools, but you fix a broken friendship with open conversation and empathy. Trying to fix a friendship with mechanical tools will only cause harm.
